original.advise_catalyst: Brilliance is mostly patience with good storage. Keep one slow project that grows monthly, a course, a craft, a language, and refuse to rush it. Finish books. Choose one person to learn from properly this year and stay teachable.

repFields.function.definition_catalyst: Wood is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is how your fuel accumulates: skills stacked, books finished, friendships tended, people learned from over years. What you gather quietly becomes what you later spend as brilliance.
repFields.function.definition_friction: Wood is your Mind, and as a friction, it is more fuel than one flame can use: courses, books, mentors, plans, all of it feeding a fire that burns hotter than it burns long.
repFields.function.advise_friction: You start more than you finish. Finish the one project closest to done this month, as it is, and let it ship at eighty percent. Put every new course, book or plan on a list until that one is out. When the urge to start something rises, ask which unfinished thing it would replace.
repFields.mechanism.base: Wood is warm by nature and fire sleeps inside it, the classics say, so every flame is fed by what was gathered before it: dry branches, stacked seasons, years of quiet growth surrendered to one bright hour. A fire is only ever as tall as its fuel. The blaze borrows everything from the forest.
repFields.mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the flame eats scraps: brilliance flaring on no reserves, warmth borrowed from tomorrow. Your chart asks you to stack wood. Learn, gather, befriend, store.
repFields.mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the fire outgrows its hearth: every branch thrown on at once, heat spent in a rush, ash by morning. Burn one pile at a time.
repFields.cta_verdict: Your mind gathers fuel long before it flares, and the ideas you feed patiently become the insights people call sudden.
repFields.carry.catalyst: The flame eats scraps: brilliance flaring on no reserves, warmth borrowed from tomorrow. Learn, gather, befriend, store.
repFields.carry.friction: The fire outgrows its hearth: every branch thrown on at once, heat spent in a rush. Burn one pile at a time.
repFields.carry.wide: You were given plenty of Wood, the fuel your light was waiting for. Burn what you have gathered. Light one thing this week.
repFields.carry.missing: No fuel behind the flame: brilliance on nothing, warmth borrowed from tomorrow. Borrow wood: learn, gather, store.
repFields.carry.spared: Wood runs absent, and the fire keeps its size: one flame, one task, burned to the end. Keep it. Gather only what you will burn.
repFields.carry.thin: Wood runs thin and unwanted: a small pile, easily burned. Burn it as it comes.
repFields.carry.excess: Too much wood feeds the fire past its task: a blaze that eats a season's fuel overnight. Bank the fire. Save half the wood.
